title: EU AI Act Article 17 Quality Management System — What High-Risk Providers Must Document by August 2, 2026
context: 2026-08-28 engine cycle — Article 17 QMS duty is binding for Annex III high-risk systems from August 2, 2026; providers must have a documented QMS covering strategy, techniques, procedures, and instructions
body: EU AI Act Article 17 requires every provider of a high-risk AI system to establish a documented quality management system that covers the full lifecycle of the AI system. This is not an optional ISO bolt-on — it is a statutory obligation binding from August 2, 2026 for Annex III high-risk systems. The QMS must include, at minimum: (1) a regulatory-compliance strategy with documented design and design-verification procedures; (2) techniques, procedures, and systematic actions for the design control, design verification, and development of the AI system; (3) examination, test, and validation procedures to be carried out before, during, and after development, with a documented frequency; (4) technical specifications including standards to be applied, and procedures for managing deviations from those standards; (5) systems and procedures for data management including data collection, data preparation, data labelling, data quality assurance, and data governance; (6) the risk management system described in Article 9, integrated into the QMS as a continuous iterative loop; (7) post-market monitoring under Article 61, configured to feed deviation events back into the QMS; (8) procedures for reporting serious incidents and malfunctioning under Article 62; (9) record-keeping procedures to demonstrate conformity with the AI Act throughout the system's lifetime; and (10) procedures for communicating with competent authorities, notified bodies, other economic operators, customers, and interested parties. The Council of AI maps the QMS directly to measured containment: each QMS procedure that controls a risk must produce a signed measurement that shows the control is in effect. A QMS manual that says 'we review bias quarterly' is self-asserted; a QMS whose bias-review control produces a dated, independently signed measurement credential over the actual review output is auditable evidence. Honest framing: monitored containment, not provable isolation. The QMS does not prove the system is safe — it proves you are watching the safety surface with a documented, signed trail. Concretely: (a) map each Article 17 QMS procedure to a measurement axis; (b) instrument the procedure to produce a signed output on a documented schedule; (c) file each signed measurement into the Council Signal Containment Incident Index for traceability; (d) feed QMS deviation events into the Article 9 risk-management loop. For small providers who find the full ISO 42001 / EN ISO 13485 pattern heavy, the Council of AI maintains an OSCAL-mapped QMS template that slots straight into a notified-body review.
